In Florida, the reinsurance tower is the policy.

When a named storm lands, the structure behind the policy pays the claim. We rebuild that catastrophe tower every June 1, layering our own retention, the Florida Hurricane Catastrophe Fund, a panel of highly rated and collateralized reinsurers, and catastrophe bonds in the capital markets.

Carrier retention at the base, the in the middle, and a panel of traditional reinsurers above it, with catastrophe bonds layered throughout. Every program is built to exceed the Florida statutory minimum.
The traditional layers are placed with reinsurers rated A− or better by AM Best, or fully collateralized. A broad panel keeps concentration with any single counterparty low.
Participating in the state catastrophe fund lowers our cost of capital against the surplus-lines market, and that edge flows through to how we price the risk.

The catastrophe tower is rebuilt every June 1. Financial strength rated A (Exceptional) by Demotech and A (Stable) by KBRA. Current program detail is filed with the SEC and posted at investors.amcoastal.com (opens in new tab) .
How the catastrophe tower is built
We don’t sell direct. Two MGAs feed every submission.
Exclusive MGA for our condominium and HOA business.
One of the largest MGAs in the country, specializing in hurricane-exposed properties.
Exclusive MGA for our apartment and assisted living business.
An MGA focused on catastrophe-exposed risk, running a proprietary risk-scored underwriting portal.

WSIA member. American Coastal Insurance Company is a member of the Wholesale & Specialty Insurance Association (opens in new tab) , the trade body for the wholesale, specialty, and surplus lines market. The membership reflects how we distribute: AmRisc, Skyway, and the E&S program underway through Skyway all place business in that market.
The team that runs the carrier.
Owns underwriting strategy, risk selection, and portfolio performance across the book.
Leads finance, treasury, reinsurance, and the rating-agency relationships.
Oversees compliance, enterprise risk, and internal audit, and serves on the carrier board.

Florida Statute 627.0629. Hurricane mitigation premium discounts are available to eligible policyholders. Information describing the discounts available under Florida law is published by the Florida Office of Insurance Regulation. View hurricane mitigation discount information (opens in new tab) .

pages.raw_title: About the Carrier | American Coastal Insurance
pages.raw_meta: American Coastal Insurance Company is Florida's largest admitted voluntary commercial residential carrier. Founded 2007, St. Petersburg, FL. Parent: American Coastal Insurance Corporation (Nasdaq: ACIC).
raw_blocks: American Coastal Insurance Company is the largest of commercial residential property in Florida. We write condominium, homeowner association, apartment, and assisted living business through two exclusive MGAs: AmRisc Group and Skyway Underwriters. We’ve done it since 2007.
The company is a wholly owned subsidiary of American Coastal Insurance Corporation, publicly traded on Nasdaq under ACIC.

The Florida commercial residential book is the anchor, not the boundary. American Coastal also assumes up to 5% of AmRisc’s E&S portfolio and supports the Skyway E&S program, applying the same catastrophe underwriting discipline to adjacent specialty property classes.

Catastrophe reinsurance is built to exceed the Florida minimum, designed to meet or exceed protection levels for AM Best A-rated carriers. The tower is placed with A− or better rated reinsurers, or fully collateralized placements, plus participation in the Florida Hurricane Catastrophe Fund.
The team that runs the carrier.
Owns underwriting strategy, risk selection, and portfolio performance across the book.
Leads finance, treasury, reinsurance, and the rating-agency relationships.
Oversees compliance, enterprise risk, and internal audit, and serves on the carrier board.
Demotech and KBRA, with WSIA and specialty-market context.
The carrier's officers and board.
Open roles posted through Paylocity.
